**Basis:** 10-K filed 2025-10-31 (period 2025-09-27); 10-Q for period 2026-06-27.

- **What It Does:** Apple sells iPhone smartphones, Mac computers, iPad tablets, Apple Watch and other wearables, AirPods, spatial computers, home products, accessories, advertising, AppleCare, cloud, payment, and other services. [extended-sec-edgar-aapl-10k]

- **Purchase Recurrence:** Hardware purchases are generally tied to product introductions and seasonal demand. Services create continuing customer commitments; as of June 27, 2026, Apple reported $14.9 billion of deferred revenue, with 64% expected to be recognized within one year. The excerpts do not provide renewal or repeat-purchase rates. [extended-sec-edgar-aapl-10q] [extended-sec-edgar-aapl-10k]

- **Recession Cyclicality:** Apple says its results depend significantly on global and regional economic conditions, so weaker economies can hurt demand and results. Sales are also seasonal, with the first fiscal quarter usually benefiting from holiday demand. [extended-sec-edgar-aapl-10k] [extended-sec-edgar-aapl-10q]
- **Management Track Record:** The supplied excerpts do not provide a complete management track record. The 2025 Form 10-K discusses year-to-year results for 2025 and 2024, while the latest 10-Q refers readers to earlier filings for additional comparisons. - **Capital Allocation:** The 2025 Form 10-K reported $132.4 billion of cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities as of September 27, 2025. [extended-sec-edgar-aapl-10k]
- **Company-specific KPIs:** For the nine months ended June 27, 2026, Apple reported net income of $101.464 billion, compared with $84.544 billion in the prior-year period. As of June 27, 2026, deferred revenue was $14.9 billion; Apple expected 64% to be recognized within one year, 23% within one to two years, 11% within two to three years, and 2% later. [extended-sec-edgar-aapl-10q]
- **Disclosed Risk Factors:** Key disclosed risks include dependence on some single or limited component suppliers, industry-wide shortages, higher component costs, commodity price changes, tariffs and other trade measures, global economic weakness, currency movements, and Apple’s international supply chain and sales exposure.
